statement: Let S be the set of products of all monotone paths from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) that move only right or down, where the product of a path is the product of grid[i][j] over all cells (i,j) visited by the path. The function returns a result r. If S has no element p with p >= 0, then r = -1. Otherwise r = (max {p in S | p >= 0}) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns some result r; it does not fail because of overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or any other panic.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r < 1000000007.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns r = -1 if and only if every monotone path from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) moving only right or down has a strictly negative product, where the product of a path is the product of grid[i][j] over all cells visited by the path.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let gridT be the n by m matrix defined by gridT[j][i] = grid[i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Then max_product_path(gridT) = max_product_path(grid).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let gridR be the m by n matrix defined by gridR[i][j] = grid[m-1-i][n-1-j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Then max_product_path(gridR) = max_product_path(grid).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a monotone path from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) moving only right or down whose product P satisfies P >= 0 and P mod 1000000007 = r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The matrix is rectangular with 1 <= m <= 15, 1 <= n <= 15, every row grid[i] has length n, and -4 <= grid[i][j] <= 4 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
